Before use: Which extra TUN features in the VPN App should be disabled?

Please disable any TUN features in your VPN app that conflict with routing or network interfaces (e.g., Exclusive TUN, Block LAN, Force Global Takeover, depending on client).\n\nThis module relies on the system tun interface and routing tables. Stacking proprietary LAN blocks prevents tethering traffic from entering the Linux forwarding path.

Yes, and it is the easiest setup.

Most hotspot clients receive a private 192.168.x address by default, and return routes are managed by Android. Enabling IPv4 and disabling IPv6 works reliably.

Simply select IPv4 in the Protocol Stack.
What should I watch out for when using IPv6?

All three conditions must be met:

1. The VPN client itself must support IPv6 (with assigned IPv6 address and routes in the tunnel).
2. IPv6 must be checked in this module's Protocol Stack.
3. Tethering hardware acceleration must be turned off (see next item); otherwise chipsets may bypass Linux routing.

If using IPv6 without IPv4, ensure all 3 points are confirmed.
Why turn off Tethering Hardware Acceleration?

When hardware offload is enabled, traffic from tethering interfaces (e.g. wlan1) may be directly offloaded to cellular hardware, bypassing the Linux network stack.

Effects:
• ip rules and module routes will not see packets
• iptables FORWARD and TCPMSS rules will not take effect
• IPv6 will frequently fail or bypass VPN

How to disable (MIUI / Xiaomi):
Settings → Additional settings → Developer options → in the Networking section, turn off "Tethering hardware acceleration" (Chinese UI label: 网络共享硬件加速).

Or via adb:
settings put global tether_offload_disabled 1
How to choose between Global, Whitelist, and Blacklist?

• Global: Routes all private subnet traffic without selecting interfaces or per-device setup.
• Whitelist: Select managed interfaces; only listed clients route through VPN.
• Blacklist: Select managed interfaces; listed clients route directly, others through VPN.

Whitelist/Blacklist require selecting managed interfaces to install iif rules.
IPv6 failed previously but now works?

Common factors:

1. Return routing: Android system must have the hotspot prefix route in local_network (table 97).
2. Hardware acceleration bypassed Linux.
3. TCPMSS clamping must precede ACCEPT to prevent PMTU black holes.
4. VPN client lacked proper IPv6 upstream routing.
